name: Elkanah
summary: Elkanah son of Jeroham, a man of Ramathaim-zophim in the hill country of Ephraim, went up yearly to worship at Shiloh. He had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah, and loved the childless Hannah tenderly. After Samuel's birth he let Hannah fulfil her vow and give the boy to the LORD's service.
catholic: Elkanah is remembered for his gentle love toward his barren wife ('Am I not better to you than ten sons?') and for his faithful yearly pilgrimage, the setting in which Hannah's prayer was heard. The Chronicler lists him among the Levites, so Samuel's priestly ministry has a family background.
know: Father of Samuel and of three more sons and two daughters by Hannah
1 Chronicles 6 counts him among the Kohathite Levites

name: Hannah
summary: Hannah, the beloved but childless wife of Elkanah, poured out her soul in silent prayer at the sanctuary of Shiloh and vowed that a son would be given to the LORD. Eli first mistook her for drunk, then blessed her. She bore Samuel, weaned him, and brought him to Eli to serve at Shiloh, singing a song of praise that celebrates God who lifts up the lowly.
catholic: Hannah's Song (1 Sam 2:1-10) is the clearest Old Testament model of Mary's Magnificat (Lk 1:46-55): both rejoice in God who humbles the proud, exalts the lowly and fills the hungry, and the Church prays Hannah's canticle in the Liturgy of the Hours. The Catechism names Hannah among the holy women whose mission prepared for Mary's (CCC 489) and says the young Samuel learned from her how to stand before the LORD (CCC 2578). Her persevering, wordless prayer is a classic example of prayer from the heart, and her offering of her child foreshadows the Presentation of Jesus in the Temple.
know: Prayed so fervently at Shiloh that Eli thought she was drunk
Dedicated Samuel to the LORD as a Nazirite-like servant
Her Song (1 Sam 2:1-10) parallels Mary's Magnificat
Later bore three more sons and two daughters

name: Peninnah
summary: Peninnah was Elkanah's second wife, who had children and provoked the childless Hannah year after year at Shiloh.

name: Eli
summary: Eli was priest at the sanctuary of Shiloh and judged Israel forty years. He blessed Hannah's prayer and raised the boy Samuel, teaching him to answer God's call, but he failed to restrain his corrupt sons Hophni and Phinehas, and a man of God foretold the fall of his house. When news came that the Ark was captured and his sons dead, the ninety-eight-year-old Eli fell backward and died.
catholic: The Catechism notes that Samuel learned from Eli the priest how to listen to God's word: 'Speak, LORD, for your servant is listening' (CCC 2578) - Eli's counsel became a model for discernment and vocational prayer, read on the 2nd Sunday in Ordinary Time (Year B). His story is also a sober warning about a shepherd who honours his children above God (1 Sam 2:29), and the prophecy against his house is fulfilled when Solomon removes Abiathar from the priesthood (1 Kgs 2:27).
know: Priest at Shiloh, where the Ark rested
Taught Samuel to say 'Speak, LORD, for your servant hears'
Did not restrain his sons' sins against the offerings
Died on hearing the Ark had been captured

name: Hophni
summary: Hophni, son of Eli, was a priest at Shiloh who with his brother Phinehas treated the LORD's offerings with contempt. Both died on the same day when the Philistines captured the Ark at Aphek.
know: Called 'worthless men' who did not know the LORD
Took the people's sacrifices by force
Died with his brother in battle as foretold

name: Phinehas
summary: Phinehas, son of Eli (not the zealous grandson of Aaron), was a corrupt priest at Shiloh who died with his brother Hophni when the Ark was captured. On hearing the news his wife went into labour and named their son Ichabod, 'the glory has departed from Israel'.
know: Son of Eli; brother of Hophni
Abused the sacrifices and the women serving at the sanctuary

name: Ichabod
summary: Ichabod was born the day the Ark was captured; his dying mother named him 'no glory', saying the glory had departed from Israel.
know: His name means roughly 'Where is the glory?'

name: Ahitub
summary: Ahitub, son of Phinehas and grandson of Eli, was the father of the priests Ahijah and Ahimelech of Nob.
know: Father of Ahimelech, the priest of Nob

name: Ahijah
summary: Ahijah son of Ahitub, great-grandson of Eli, wore the ephod and was with Saul at Gibeah during the battle of Michmash.
know: Carried the ephod in Saul's camp
Possibly the same person as Ahimelech of Nob

name: Ahimelech
summary: Ahimelech son of Ahitub, priest at Nob, gave the fleeing David the holy showbread and Goliath's sword. Doeg the Edomite reported it, and Saul had Ahimelech and eighty-five priests of Nob slaughtered; only his son Abiathar escaped to David.
catholic: Jesus cites this episode (Mt 12:3-4; Mk 2:25-26) to show that mercy and human need come before ritual law and that he, Son of David, is Lord of the Sabbath. Mark's account names the high priest of that time as Abiathar, Ahimelech's son. The holy bread given to David is often read by the Fathers as a figure of the Eucharistic bread.
know: Murdered with the priests of Nob on Saul's order

name: Abiathar
summary: Abiathar son of Ahimelech alone escaped Saul's massacre of the priests of Nob and fled to David with the ephod. He served as priest beside Zadok throughout David's reign and stayed loyal during Absalom's revolt, but backed Adonijah's bid for the throne; Solomon spared his life but banished him to Anathoth, fulfilling the word spoken against Eli's house.
catholic: Abiathar's removal marks the end of Eli's priestly line and the rise of Zadok's, which Ezekiel later names as the faithful priesthood. Mark 2:26 recalls 'the time of Abiathar the high priest' when David ate the showbread, a passage Jesus uses to teach that the Sabbath is made for man.
know: Sole survivor of the massacre at Nob
Sided with Adonijah and was exiled to Anathoth

name: Jonathan son of Abiathar
summary: Jonathan, son of Abiathar the priest, ran messages to David during Absalom's revolt and later brought Adonijah the news that Solomon had been made king.
know: Hid in a well at Bahurim with Ahimaaz
Announced Solomon's anointing to Adonijah's feast

name: Samuel
summary: Samuel, son of Elkanah and Hannah, was given to the LORD as a child and grew up at Shiloh under Eli, where God called him by name in the night. He became prophet, priest-like intercessor and the last judge of Israel, leading the people back to God at Mizpah. At the people's demand he anointed Saul as first king, later rebuked Saul's disobedience, and secretly anointed the boy David at Bethlehem.
catholic: Samuel's night-time call ('Speak, LORD, for your servant is listening') is the Church's favourite text on vocation and listening prayer; the Catechism says he learned to pray from Hannah and Eli (CCC 2578). Scripture ranks him with Moses as a great intercessor (Ps 99:6; Jer 15:1), and Peter calls him the first of the prophets who foretold Christ's days (Acts 3:24). By anointing David he stands at the head of the line of the Anointed (Messiah/Christ) king (CCC 436). The Roman Martyrology commemorates the holy prophet Samuel on August 20.
know: Called by God as a boy in the temple at Shiloh
Last of the judges; a prophet from Dan to Beersheba
His sons' corruption led Israel to ask for a king
Summoned from the dead by the medium of Endor

name: Joel son of Samuel
summary: Joel, Samuel's firstborn, judged at Beersheba but took bribes and perverted justice, prompting the elders to demand a king. Through his son Heman the singer, Samuel's line served in the Temple music.

name: Abijah son of Samuel
summary: Abijah, Samuel's second son, judged with his brother Joel at Beersheba and, like him, took bribes.
know: His corruption helped prompt Israel's request for a king

name: Heman
summary: Heman the singer, grandson of Samuel, was one of David's three chief Levite musicians with Asaph and Jeduthun, and with his sons prophesied with lyres, harps and cymbals.
catholic: With Asaph and Jeduthun, Heman stands for the ordered sung worship of the Temple that the Church's Liturgy of the Hours continues; Psalm 88 is traditionally associated with a Heman.
know: His fourteen sons served in the music

name: Abinadab of Kiriath-jearim
summary: When the Philistines returned the Ark, it was brought to Abinadab's house on the hill at Kiriath-jearim, where it remained about twenty years until David came to move it.
know: The Ark stayed in his house for decades
Father of Eleazar, Uzzah and Ahio

name: Eleazar son of Abinadab
summary: Eleazar was consecrated by the men of Kiriath-jearim to keep the Ark of the LORD in his father's house.
know: Set apart to guard the Ark

name: Uzzah
summary: Uzzah, son of Abinadab, drove the new cart carrying the Ark toward Jerusalem; when the oxen stumbled he put out his hand to steady the Ark and was struck dead.
catholic: Uzzah's death is a classic lesson in reverence for the holy: the Ark was to be carried on poles by Levites, not handled. It sets up David's fear - 'How can the Ark of the LORD come to me?' - which Elizabeth echoes before Mary (Lk 1:43).

name: Ahio
summary: Ahio, son of Abinadab, walked ahead of the cart carrying the Ark when David first tried to bring it to Jerusalem.

name: Obed-Edom
summary: Obed-Edom the Gittite sheltered the Ark in his house for three months after Uzzah's death, and the LORD blessed his whole household; hearing this, David brought the Ark up to Jerusalem with joy.
catholic: Luke's Visitation narrative closely parallels 2 Samuel 6: as the Ark stayed three months in the house of Obed-Edom bringing blessing, Mary - the new Ark carrying the Word made flesh - stays about three months in Zechariah's house (Lk 1:56). The Catechism calls Mary 'the ark of the covenant, the place where the glory of the Lord dwells' (CCC 2676).
know: His house was blessed because of the Ark
Parallels Mary's three-month stay with Elizabeth

relations.type: type of (three months with the Ark)

name: Abiel
summary: Abiel, a Benjaminite, was the father of Kish (Saul's father) and of Ner (Abner's father).
know: Grandfather of both Saul and Abner

name: Kish
summary: Kish son of Abiel was a wealthy Benjaminite of Gibeah; Saul met Samuel while searching for his father's lost donkeys.

name: Ner
summary: Ner son of Abiel was Saul's uncle and the father of Abner, Saul's army commander.

name: Abner
summary: Abner son of Ner, Saul's cousin, commanded Saul's army and after Saul's death made Ishbosheth king over Israel. He killed Asahel in battle, then quarrelled with Ishbosheth and went over to David, but Joab murdered him at Hebron in revenge; David mourned him publicly.
know: Introduced the young David to Saul after Goliath
Murdered by Joab in the gate of Hebron

name: Saul
summary: Saul son of Kish, a tall young Benjaminite, was anointed by Samuel as Israel's first king and began well, rescuing Jabesh-gilead. But he offered sacrifice without waiting for Samuel and spared Agag and the spoil of Amalek, so the LORD rejected him as king. Tormented by an evil spirit and jealousy of David, he hunted David for years, consulted a medium at Endor, and died with three sons on Mount Gilboa.
catholic: Saul shows that anointing is a gift that requires obedience: 'to obey is better than sacrifice' (1 Sam 15:22). As the first anointed king he stands at the start of the line of the 'messiah', the Anointed One, fulfilled in Christ (CCC 436). Fathers such as Augustine contrast proud Saul with humble David, and Saul of Tarsus - named after him and of the same tribe - recalls him in his sermon at Antioch (Acts 13:21). David's refusal to harm 'the LORD's anointed' is read on the 7th Sunday in Ordinary Time (Year C) as a model of love of enemies.
know: Died by his own sword on Mount Gilboa

name: Ahinoam daughter of Ahimaaz
summary: Ahinoam daughter of Ahimaaz is the only named wife of King Saul.
know: Not the same as David's wife Ahinoam of Jezreel

name: Jonathan
summary: Jonathan, Saul's eldest son, was a brave warrior who with only his armour-bearer routed a Philistine garrison at Michmash. He loved David 'as his own soul', made a covenant with him, gave him his robe and weapons, and warned him of Saul's plots, accepting that David, not he, would be king. He died beside his father on Mount Gilboa, and David lamented him and later cared for his son Mephibosheth.
catholic: The friendship of David and Jonathan is the Bible's great portrait of covenant friendship: self-giving, faithful and rooted in God. Jonathan's yielding of his own claim to the throne to God's chosen one is often compared with John the Baptist's 'He must increase, I must decrease'. David's lament (2 Sam 1:17-27) is one of the most moving elegies in Scripture.
know: Victory at Michmash with his armour-bearer
Made a covenant of friendship with David
Gave David his robe, sword and bow
Died on Mount Gilboa with Saul

name: Malchishua
summary: Malchishua, a son of Saul, was killed by the Philistines with his father and brothers on Mount Gilboa.

name: Abinadab son of Saul
summary: Abinadab, a son of Saul, died with his father on Mount Gilboa.

name: Ishbosheth
summary: Ishbosheth, a son of Saul, was made king over Israel at Mahanaim by Abner and reigned two years while David ruled Judah at Hebron. After he accused Abner over Saul's concubine Rizpah, Abner defected; Ishbosheth was then murdered in his bed by Rechab and Baanah, whom David executed.
know: Reigned two years over the northern tribes
Murdered by two of his own captains

name: Merab
summary: Merab, Saul's elder daughter, was promised to David but given instead to Adriel the Meholathite; her five sons were later handed to the Gibeonites.
know: Promised to David, married to Adriel

name: Adriel
summary: Adriel the Meholathite, son of Barzillai, married Saul's daughter Merab.
know: Not the same Barzillai as David's Gileadite friend

name: Michal
role: Daughter of Saul, wife of David
summary: Michal, Saul's younger daughter, loved David and became his wife; she saved him by letting him down through a window and deceiving Saul's men with an idol in the bed. Saul gave her to Paltiel, but David reclaimed her when he became king. When she despised David for dancing before the Ark, Scripture notes she had no child to the day of her death.
catholic: Michal's contempt for David's joyful, humble dancing before the Ark contrasts with the joy that greets the new Ark in Luke 1, where John leaps in Elizabeth's womb before Mary. Spiritual writers use her as an image of pride that cannot rejoice in God's presence.
know: Loved David and saved his life
Given to Paltiel, then returned to David
Despised David's dancing before the Ark

name: Paltiel
summary: Paltiel (Palti) son of Laish received Michal from Saul; when she was taken back to David he followed her weeping as far as Bahurim.
know: Wept as Michal was taken from him

name: Rizpah
summary: Rizpah daughter of Aiah was Saul's concubine. When her two sons were executed by the Gibeonites, she kept vigil over their bodies on a rock from the beginning of harvest until the rains, guarding them from birds and beasts; her devotion moved David to give Saul's house honourable burial.
catholic: Rizpah's long vigil over her dead sons is often seen as an icon of a mother's sorrowing fidelity, recalling the Mother standing at the Cross.
know: Guarded her sons' bodies for months

name: Armoni
summary: Armoni, son of Saul and Rizpah, was handed to the Gibeonites and executed to atone for Saul's slaughter of Gibeon.
know: One of seven descendants of Saul executed at Gibeah

name: Mephibosheth son of Saul
summary: This Mephibosheth, son of Saul and Rizpah, was executed by the Gibeonites; he is distinct from Jonathan's lame son of the same name.

name: Mephibosheth
summary: Mephibosheth, Jonathan's son, was lamed at five when his nurse fled with him at news of Gilboa. David, keeping his covenant with Jonathan, restored Saul's land to him and had him eat at the king's table always. During Absalom's revolt his servant Ziba accused him of disloyalty; on David's return he came out unwashed in mourning, and David divided the land between them.
catholic: Mephibosheth at the king's table is a favourite image of grace: a lame, powerless heir of a fallen house invited, for another's sake, to eat always with the king - an image of the sinner welcomed to the Eucharistic table for Christ's sake. His story shows David's hesed (covenant kindness).
know: Lame in both feet from childhood
Ate at David's table for Jonathan's sake

name: Mica
summary: Mica, young son of Mephibosheth, carried on the line of Saul and Jonathan.

name: Ziba
summary: Ziba, a servant of Saul's house, told David of Mephibosheth and managed his land; during Absalom's revolt he brought supplies to David and falsely accused his master, winning half the estate.
know: Had fifteen sons and twenty servants

name: Rechab son of Rimmon
summary: Rechab, a captain of Ishbosheth, killed the sleeping king with his brother Baanah and brought his head to David, who had them executed.

name: Baanah son of Rimmon
summary: Baanah, Rechab's brother, shared in the murder of Ishbosheth and was executed by David.

name: Medium of Endor
summary: On the eve of his last battle Saul, in disguise, asked a woman at Endor who had a familiar spirit to bring up Samuel; Samuel appeared and foretold Saul's death and Israel's defeat.
catholic: Saul's visit breaks the law he himself had enforced against mediums (1 Sam 28:3; Deut 18:10-12). The Church teaches that all recourse to mediums and conjuring the dead must be rejected (CCC 2116). Sirach 46:20 says Samuel prophesied after his death.

name: Agag
summary: Agag king of the Amalekites was spared by Saul against God's command; Samuel himself put him to death at Gilgal.
know: His sparing cost Saul the kingdom
Haman in Esther is called an Agagite

name: Nahash
summary: Nahash the Ammonite besieged Jabesh-gilead, demanding to gouge out every right eye; Saul's rescue of the city confirmed his kingship. Nahash later showed kindness to David.

name: Hanun
summary: Hanun son of Nahash humiliated David's envoys of condolence, shaving half their beards, which provoked the Ammonite war in which Uriah later died.

name: Doeg
summary: Doeg the Edomite, Saul's chief herdsman, saw Ahimelech help David at Nob, informed Saul, and when Saul's guards refused, himself slaughtered the priests of Nob and the town.
know: Informer and executioner of the priests
Psalm 52 is traditionally linked to him

name: Achish
summary: Achish king of Gath twice received David as a fugitive - first David feigned madness before him, later he gave David the town of Ziklag - but the Philistine lords refused to let David fight against Israel.

name: Goliath
summary: Goliath of Gath, a giant Philistine champion, defied the armies of Israel for forty days until the shepherd boy David, trusting in the LORD, felled him with a stone from his sling and cut off his head with the giant's own sword.
catholic: The Fathers read David's victory over Goliath as a figure of Christ's victory over Satan: the humble shepherd from Bethlehem defeats the proud enemy with the weakest means, 'that all the earth may know there is a God in Israel'. Augustine and Caesarius of Arles preached on this typology.
know: About six cubits and a span tall
His sword was later kept at Nob

name: Elhanan
summary: Elhanan son of Jaare-Oregim (Jair in Chronicles), a Bethlehemite, killed a giant of Gath at Gob - in this translation 'Goliath the Gittite's brother', named Lahmi in 1 Chronicles 20:5.
know: The Hebrew of 2 Sam 21:19 literally reads that he killed Goliath; translations follow 1 Chr 20:5
One of David's champions against the Philistine giants

name: David
summary: David, youngest son of Jesse of Bethlehem, was a shepherd anointed by Samuel, who killed Goliath, served and fled from Saul, and became king first of Judah at Hebron and then of all Israel. He captured Jerusalem, brought the Ark there with dancing and joy, and received God's covenant promise of an everlasting dynasty (2 Sam 7). He sinned gravely with Bathsheba and against Uriah, repented when Nathan confronted him, and suffered rebellion within his own house, especially Absalom's. He reigned forty years and prepared for the Temple his son Solomon would build.
catholic: David is a principal type of Christ: the shepherd-king born in Bethlehem, anointed with the Spirit, rejected before being enthroned. God's covenant through Nathan - 'your throne shall be established for ever' (2 Sam 7:16) - is fulfilled when Gabriel tells Mary that God will give her son 'the throne of his father David' (Lk 1:32-33); 'Son of David' is the messianic title the crowds give Jesus (CCC 439). The Catechism calls David 'par excellence the king after God's own heart', a shepherd who prays for his people, whose submission to God's will, praise and repentance are a model of prayer (CCC 2579); Psalm 51, the Miserere, is the Church's great penitential psalm. His dancing before the Ark is echoed in the Visitation, when the unborn John leaps before Mary, the new Ark (CCC 2676). The Roman Martyrology commemorates holy King David on December 29.
know: Youngest son of Jesse; a shepherd of Bethlehem
Made Jerusalem his capital and brought the Ark there
Jesus is hailed as 'Son of David'

name: Eliab
summary: Eliab, Jesse's firstborn, was so impressive that Samuel thought him the LORD's anointed, but God 'looks at the heart'. At the Valley of Elah he scolded David for coming to the battle.

name: Abinadab son of Jesse
summary: Abinadab, Jesse's second son, was passed over by Samuel and served in Saul's army against Goliath.

name: Shammah son of Jesse
summary: Shammah (also Shimea, Shimeah or Shimei), Jesse's third son, was passed over by Samuel and fought in Saul's army; his sons Jonadab and Jonathan appear in David's story.

name: Nethanel son of Jesse
summary: Nethanel is listed as Jesse's fourth son.

name: Raddai
summary: Raddai is listed as Jesse's fifth son.

name: Ozem
summary: Ozem is listed as Jesse's sixth son, David being the seventh.

name: Zeruiah
summary: Zeruiah, David's sister, was the mother of his three fierce commanders Abishai, Joab and Asahel, who are usually named after her.
know: Her sons are called 'sons of Zeruiah'
David found them 'too hard' for him

name: Abigail, sister of David
summary: Abigail, sister of David and Zeruiah, was the mother of Amasa by Jether (Ithra); 2 Samuel calls her the daughter of Nahash.

name: Jether
summary: Jether (Ithra), called an Ishmaelite in Chronicles and an Israelite in Samuel, fathered Amasa by David's sister Abigail.

name: Jonadab
summary: Jonadab son of Shimeah, a 'very subtle man', advised his cousin Amnon how to trap Tamar, and later told David that only Amnon had been killed by Absalom.

name: Jonathan son of Shimei
summary: Jonathan, son of David's brother Shimei (Shimea), killed a six-fingered giant of Gath.

name: Joab
summary: Joab son of Zeruiah, David's nephew, led the capture of Jerusalem and commanded David's army for decades. Loyal but ruthless, he murdered Abner and Amasa, arranged Uriah's death at David's command, engineered Absalom's return and then killed him against orders. He backed Adonijah, and Solomon had him executed at the altar.
know: Carried out David's order to place Uriah in the front line
Executed by Benaiah at Solomon's command

name: Abishai
summary: Abishai son of Zeruiah went with David into Saul's camp and wanted to kill the sleeping king, but David refused to touch the LORD's anointed. He later commanded part of the army, offered to kill Shimei, and rescued David from a Philistine giant.

name: Asahel
summary: Asahel son of Zeruiah, 'as light of foot as a wild gazelle', pursued Abner after the battle of Gibeon and was killed by him, which Joab later avenged.

name: Amasa
summary: Amasa, David's nephew, commanded Absalom's rebel army; David forgave him and made him commander in Joab's place, but Joab treacherously stabbed him while greeting him with a kiss.

name: Abigail
summary: Abigail, the intelligent and beautiful wife of the churlish Nabal of Carmel, rode out with gifts to meet David when he was coming to take revenge on her household, and by her humble, wise words kept him from bloodguilt. After Nabal died, David married her; she was captured at Ziklag and rescued, and bore David's son Chileab (Daniel).
catholic: Abigail's intercession - she takes the blame upon herself and turns away the anger of the future king - has led spiritual writers to see in her a figure of Mary the intercessor and a model of peacemaking. Her speech confesses David's 'sure house' before Nathan's oracle (1 Sam 25:28).
know: Wife of Nabal, then of David

name: Nabal
summary: Nabal ('fool'), a rich and surly man of Maon with flocks at Carmel, insulted David's men; after Abigail's intercession he was struck by the LORD and died.
know: Died ten days after hearing what Abigail had done

name: Ahinoam of Jezreel
summary: Ahinoam of Jezreel married David during his fugitive years, was captured and rescued at Ziklag, and bore his firstborn son Amnon at Hebron.

name: Maacah
summary: Maacah, daughter of Talmai king of Geshur, bore David his sons Absalom and (by implication) Tamar.

name: Talmai
summary: Talmai son of Ammihud, king of Geshur, was David's father-in-law; Absalom took refuge with him for three years after killing Amnon.

name: Haggith
summary: Haggith bore David his fourth son, Adonijah, at Hebron.

name: Abital
summary: Abital bore David his fifth son, Shephatiah, at Hebron.

name: Eglah
summary: Eglah bore David his sixth son, Ithream, at Hebron.

name: Eliam
summary: Eliam (Ammiel in Chronicles) was Bathsheba's father; an Eliam son of Ahithophel is listed among David's mighty men, and many interpreters identify the two.
know: Possibly Ahithophel's son, which would make Ahithophel Bathsheba's grandfather

name: Bathsheba
summary: Bathsheba, daughter of Eliam and wife of Uriah the Hittite, was taken by David, who then arranged Uriah's death; their first child died. She bore Solomon and other sons, and with Nathan secured Solomon's succession against Adonijah. As queen mother she sat on a throne at King Solomon's right hand, who rose and bowed to her when she came to intercede.
catholic: Bathsheba is the clearest biblical example of the gebirah, the queen mother of the Davidic kingdom: the king rises to meet her, bows, and sets a throne for her at his right hand (1 Kgs 2:19). Catholic theology sees here a type of Mary's queenship: the mother of the Son of David reigns beside her Son and intercedes with him, as Mary is 'exalted by the Lord as Queen over all things' (CCC 966) and Christ's kingdom is the fulfilment of David's. Matthew's genealogy names her discreetly as 'her who had been Uriah's wife' (Mt 1:6), one of the four women before Mary.
know: Wife of Uriah, then of David
Mother of Solomon (and of Shimea, Shobab and Nathan)
Sat at the king's right hand as queen mother

name: Uriah
summary: Uriah the Hittite, one of David's Thirty mighty men, refused to go home to his wife while the Ark and army were in the field. David then sent him back to Joab carrying the letter that arranged his death at Rabbah.
catholic: Uriah's loyalty and integrity throw David's sin into sharp relief; Matthew's genealogy keeps his name before the Messiah's ('her who had been Uriah's wife'), a reminder that Christ entered a history marked by sin to redeem it.
know: A Hittite in David's elite guard
Would not go home while the army camped
Carried his own death warrant to Joab

name: Amnon
summary: Amnon, David's firstborn, became obsessed with his half-sister Tamar, raped her by a ruse and then hated her. Two years later her brother Absalom had him killed at a sheep-shearing feast.

name: Chileab
summary: Chileab, David's second son, born of Abigail at Hebron, is called Daniel in Chronicles; nothing else is recorded of him.

name: Absalom
summary: Absalom, David's handsome third son by Maacah, avenged his sister Tamar by killing Amnon and fled to Geshur. Restored through Joab, he won the hearts of Israel and raised a revolt at Hebron, driving David from Jerusalem and taking his concubines. Defeated in the forest of Ephraim, he was caught by his hair in an oak and killed by Joab, and David wept, 'O my son Absalom!'
catholic: David's grief over Absalom - 'would that I had died instead of you' - is often read as an image of the Father's love for rebellious children. The Mount of Olives ascent of the weeping, barefoot David betrayed by his son and his counsellor Ahithophel (2 Sam 15:30-31) is read by the Fathers as a figure of Christ's agony and betrayal on the same mount.
know: Stole the hearts of Israel at the gate
Died hanging from an oak, killed by Joab

name: Adonijah
role: Son of David, claimant to the throne
summary: Adonijah, David's fourth son by Haggith, tried to make himself king as David lay dying, backed by Joab and Abiathar. Nathan and Bathsheba secured Solomon's anointing instead; Adonijah was spared, but when he asked for David's companion Abishag as wife, Solomon saw a claim to the throne and had him executed.
know: Clung to the horns of the altar

name: Shephatiah
summary: Shephatiah was David's fifth son, born of Abital at Hebron.

name: Ithream
summary: Ithream was David's sixth son, born of Eglah at Hebron.

name: Shammua
summary: Shammua (Shimea), born in Jerusalem, is listed first among Bathsheba's four sons.

name: Shobab
summary: Shobab, son of David and Bathsheba, was born in Jerusalem.

name: Nathan son of David
summary: Nathan, a son of David and Bathsheba born in Jerusalem, is otherwise unknown in the Old Testament, but Luke traces the genealogy of Jesus back to David through him rather than through Solomon.
catholic: Luke's genealogy (Lk 3:31) runs through Nathan, Matthew's through Solomon. A long tradition, found already in early writers, explains the two lines as Mary's (Luke) and Joseph's (Matthew), or as Joseph's natural and legal descent; either way both make Jesus truly 'Son of David'. Zechariah 12:12 mentions 'the family of the house of Nathan' mourning the pierced one.
know: Son of Bathsheba, full brother of Solomon
Ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy

name: Ibhar
summary: Ibhar was a son of David born in Jerusalem.

name: Elishua
summary: Elishua was a son of David born in Jerusalem (apparently called Elishama in 1 Chr 3:6).

name: Nepheg
summary: Nepheg was a son of David born in Jerusalem.

name: Japhia
summary: Japhia was a son of David born in Jerusalem.

name: Elishama
summary: Elishama was a son of David born in Jerusalem.

name: Eliada
summary: Eliada (Beeliada in 1 Chr 14:7) was a son of David born in Jerusalem.

name: Eliphelet
summary: Eliphelet was the last-named son of David born in Jerusalem.

name: Elpelet
summary: Elpelet (an earlier Eliphelet in 1 Chr 3:6) was a son of David born in Jerusalem.

name: Nogah
summary: Nogah was a son of David born in Jerusalem, listed only in Chronicles.

name: Jerimoth
summary: Jerimoth, a son of David not in the main lists (perhaps by a concubine), was the father of Rehoboam's wife Mahalath.

name: Mahalath
summary: Mahalath, granddaughter of David through Jerimoth and of Eliab through her mother Abihail, married Rehoboam and bore him three sons.
know: Both her parents were of David's family

name: Tamar
summary: Tamar, David's beautiful daughter and Absalom's full sister, was raped by her half-brother Amnon and then cast out; she lived desolate in Absalom's house, and his revenge set off the tragedies of David's later reign.
catholic: Tamar's protest - 'Don't do this folly!' - gives voice to the dignity of the victim, and the narrative honestly exposes the consequences of sin in David's house that Nathan foretold (2 Sam 12:10).
know: Wore a robe of many colours as a king's daughter

name: Tamar daughter of Absalom
summary: Absalom named his only daughter Tamar, after his sister; she was 'a woman of beautiful face'.
know: Possibly the mother of Rehoboam's wife Maacah

name: Nathan
summary: Nathan the prophet brought David God's covenant promise of an everlasting house and throne (2 Sam 7). After David's sin with Bathsheba he confronted the king with the parable of the poor man's ewe lamb - 'You are the man!' - and announced both forgiveness and its consequences. He named the infant Solomon 'Jedidiah' and, with Bathsheba, ensured Solomon succeeded David.
catholic: Nathan's oracle (2 Sam 7:12-16), read on the 4th Sunday of Advent (Year B) alongside the Annunciation, is the foundation of the Church's teaching that Christ is the promised Son of David whose kingdom has no end (Lk 1:32-33). His rebuke of David is a model of fraternal correction and prophetic courage, and David's 'I have sinned against the LORD' with Nathan's word of pardon foreshadows sacramental confession and absolution (2 Sam 12:7-13 is read on the 11th Sunday in Ordinary Time, Year C).
know: Told the parable of the ewe lamb

name: Gad
summary: Gad the prophet advised David during his flight from Saul to go into Judah. After David's sinful census he offered him a choice of three punishments and then told him to build an altar on the threshing floor of Araunah, the future Temple site.
know: Brought the choice of punishments after the census
Directed the altar on Araunah's threshing floor

name: Ahitub
summary: Ahitub son of Amariah, of the line of Eleazar son of Aaron, was the father of Zadok the priest.
know: Zadok's descent from Eleazar is traced through him

name: Zadok
summary: Zadok son of Ahitub, a priest descended from Eleazar son of Aaron, served alongside Abiathar under David and carried the Ark when David fled Absalom. He stayed loyal when Abiathar backed Adonijah, anointed Solomon king at the Gihon spring, and became sole chief priest; his descendants held the high priesthood until the Exile.
catholic: Zadok's anointing of Solomon ('Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anointed Solomon king') became part of the coronation rite of Christian kings. Ezekiel singles out 'the sons of Zadok' as the faithful priests of the restored temple (Ezek 44:15), and the Church sees in the faithful priesthood a figure of the priests of the New Covenant serving Christ.
know: Ancestor of the high priests to the Exile

name: Ahimaaz
summary: Ahimaaz son of Zadok carried secret news to David during Absalom's revolt and outran the Cushite to bring word of the victory, tactfully withholding the news of Absalom's death.
know: David called him 'a good man' with good news
Hid in a well at Bahurim

name: Benaiah
summary: Benaiah son of Jehoiada, a valiant warrior who killed a lion in a pit on a snowy day, commanded David's bodyguard (the Cherethites and Pelethites). He supported Solomon, executed Adonijah, Joab and Shimei, and became Solomon's army commander.
know: Killed a lion in a pit on a snowy day
Captain of the Cherethites and Pelethites

name: Jehoiada (father of Benaiah)
summary: Jehoiada of Kabzeel, called 'the chief priest' in 1 Chr 27:5, was the father of David's warrior Benaiah.
know: Not the later priest who crowned Joash

name: Ittai the Gittite
summary: Ittai, a Philistine of Gath newly come to David with six hundred men, refused to turn back when David fled Absalom: 'wherever my lord the king is, in death or in life, there your servant will be'. He commanded a third of David's army.
catholic: Ittai, a foreigner, pledges loyalty to the rejected king in words close to Ruth's and to Peter's 'Lord, I will go with you to death' - an image of Gentiles cleaving to the rejected Messiah.
know: Swore loyalty to David in exile
Commanded a third of the army

name: Hushai the Archite
summary: Hushai the Archite, 'David's friend', met David on the Mount of Olives during Absalom's revolt and went back as a double agent. His advice to Absalom overturned Ahithophel's sound counsel and gave David time to escape.
know: Sent intelligence to David through the priests' sons

name: Ahithophel
summary: Ahithophel the Gilonite was David's counsellor, whose advice was regarded 'as if a man inquired at the word of God'. He joined Absalom's revolt; when Absalom preferred Hushai's counsel, Ahithophel went home, set his house in order and hanged himself.
catholic: Ahithophel - the trusted friend who betrays the king and then hangs himself - is widely read by the Fathers as a type of Judas (cf. Ps 41:9, Jn 13:18). David's prayer 'turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness' is answered through Hushai.
know: His counsel was valued like an oracle

name: Shimei son of Gera
summary: Shimei, a Benjaminite of Saul's clan, cursed and stoned David as he fled Absalom; David stopped Abishai from killing him, saying the LORD may have bidden him. Pardoned on David's return, he was later confined to Jerusalem by Solomon and executed when he broke the terms.
catholic: David's meek acceptance of Shimei's curses is read as a figure of Christ who, 'when he was cursed, did not curse back' (1 Pt 2:23).
know: Executed by Solomon for leaving Jerusalem

name: Barzillai the Gileadite
summary: Barzillai, a very old and wealthy Gileadite of Rogelim, provided food for David at Mahanaim during Absalom's revolt. He declined David's invitation to live at court because of his age, sending his son Chimham instead.
know: Fed David's people in the wilderness
David commended his sons to Solomon

name: Chimham
summary: Chimham, presumably Barzillai's son, went with David to Jerusalem in his father's place.
know: A place near Bethlehem later bore his name

name: Sheba son of Bichri
summary: Sheba son of Bichri, a Benjaminite, raised a revolt of the northern tribes after Absalom's defeat; a wise woman of Abel Beth Maacah persuaded her city to throw his head over the wall to Joab.
know: Cried 'We have no portion in David'
Killed by the people of Abel

name: Abishag the Shunammite
summary: Abishag, a beautiful young woman of Shunem, was brought to nurse and warm the aged David. After David's death Adonijah's request to marry her cost him his life.
know: Attended David in his old age
Adonijah's request for her was seen as a claim to the throne

name: Araunah
summary: Araunah (Ornan) the Jebusite owned the threshing floor where the destroying angel stopped. He offered it free, but David insisted on paying, built an altar there, and the plague ended; Solomon's Temple was built on that spot.
catholic: David's words 'I will not offer to the LORD burnt offerings that cost me nothing' are a classic text on true sacrifice. The Chronicler identifies the site with Mount Moriah (2 Chr 3:1), linking Abraham's offering of Isaac, David's altar and the Temple - a typological thread Christian readers carry to Calvary.
know: Sold his threshing floor to David

name: Hadadezer
summary: Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah in Syria, was defeated by David, who took his golden shields to Jerusalem; he later aided the Ammonites against David.

name: Asaph
summary: Asaph son of Berechiah, a Levite of Gershom, was appointed by David as chief singer before the Ark with cymbals; his sons and guild served in Temple music down to the return from exile.
catholic: Twelve Psalms (50 and 73-83) are attributed to Asaph; the Church continues prayer in the Psalms of Asaph daily in the Liturgy of the Hours. Chronicles even calls him 'Asaph the seer' (2 Chr 29:30).
know: Chief of the singers before the Ark
His sons returned from exile as singers

name: Jeduthun
summary: Jeduthun was one of David's three chief Levite musicians with Asaph and Heman, whose sons prophesied with the harp in giving thanks to the LORD.
catholic: Psalms 39, 62 and 77 carry his name in their titles.

name: Jabez
summary: Jabez, 'more honourable than his brothers', was named in sorrow by his mother but prayed that God would bless him, enlarge his border and keep him from harm, 'and God granted him that which he requested'.
catholic: The short prayer of Jabez is a reminder within the genealogies that God hears personal, confident petition.
know: His prayer is recorded in the middle of a genealogy

name: Abishua
summary: Abishua is listed in the high-priestly line of Eleazar son of Aaron in 1 Chronicles 6.
know: Part of the Aaronic line from Eleazar to the Exile

name: Bukki
summary: Bukki is listed in the high-priestly line of Eleazar son of Aaron in 1 Chronicles 6.
know: Part of the Aaronic line from Eleazar to the Exile

name: Uzzi
summary: Uzzi is listed in the high-priestly line of Eleazar son of Aaron in 1 Chronicles 6.
know: Part of the Aaronic line from Eleazar to the Exile

name: Zerahiah
summary: Zerahiah is listed in the high-priestly line of Eleazar son of Aaron in 1 Chronicles 6.
know: Part of the Aaronic line from Eleazar to the Exile

name: Meraioth
summary: Meraioth is listed in the high-priestly line of Eleazar son of Aaron in 1 Chronicles 6.
know: Part of the Aaronic line from Eleazar to the Exile

name: Amariah son of Meraioth
summary: Amariah son of Meraioth is listed in the high-priestly line of Eleazar son of Aaron in 1 Chronicles 6.
know: Part of the Aaronic line from Eleazar to the Exile

name: Azariah son of Ahimaaz
summary: Azariah son of Ahimaaz is listed in the high-priestly line of Eleazar son of Aaron in 1 Chronicles 6. 1 Kings 4:2 lists an 'Azariah the son of Zadok' as Solomon's priest, probably the same man (grandson of Zadok).
know: Part of the Aaronic line from Eleazar to the Exile

name: Johanan son of Azariah
summary: Johanan son of Azariah is listed in the high-priestly line of Eleazar son of Aaron in 1 Chronicles 6.
know: Part of the Aaronic line from Eleazar to the Exile

name: Azariah son of Johanan
summary: Azariah son of Johanan is listed in the high-priestly line of Eleazar son of Aaron in 1 Chronicles 6. He is noted as the one 'who executed the priest's office in the house that Solomon built'.
know: Part of the Aaronic line from Eleazar to the Exile

name: Amariah son of Azariah
summary: Amariah son of Azariah is listed in the high-priestly line of Eleazar son of Aaron in 1 Chronicles 6. An Amariah was chief priest 'over all matters of the LORD' under Jehoshaphat (2 Chr 19:11).
know: Part of the Aaronic line from Eleazar to the Exile

name: Ahitub son of Amariah
summary: Ahitub son of Amariah is listed in the high-priestly line of Eleazar son of Aaron in 1 Chronicles 6.
know: Part of the Aaronic line from Eleazar to the Exile

name: Zadok son of Ahitub (II)
summary: Zadok son of Ahitub (II) is listed in the high-priestly line of Eleazar son of Aaron in 1 Chronicles 6.
know: Part of the Aaronic line from Eleazar to the Exile

name: Shallum son of Zadok
summary: Shallum son of Zadok is listed in the high-priestly line of Eleazar son of Aaron in 1 Chronicles 6.
know: Part of the Aaronic line from Eleazar to the Exile

name: Hilkiah
summary: Hilkiah, high priest under King Josiah, found 'the book of the law' in the Temple during its repair and gave it to Shaphan the scribe. He led the delegation to the prophetess Huldah and carried out Josiah's purge of idolatrous objects from the Temple.
catholic: The finding of the book of the law under Hilkiah - widely identified with Deuteronomy - sparked Josiah's reform and covenant renewal, a biblical example of renewal of the Church through rediscovery of the Word of God.
know: Found the book of the law in the Temple
Removed Baal's vessels from the Temple

name: Azariah son of Hilkiah
summary: Azariah son of Hilkiah is listed in the high-priestly line of Eleazar son of Aaron in 1 Chronicles 6.
know: Part of the Aaronic line from Eleazar to the Exile

name: Seraiah
summary: Seraiah, chief priest when Jerusalem fell in 587 BC, was taken by Nebuzaradan to Nebuchadnezzar at Riblah and executed. He was the father of Jehozadak, and Ezra traces his ancestry to him.
know: Last high priest of Solomon's Temple

name: Jehozadak
summary: Jehozadak son of Seraiah went into captivity when Nebuchadnezzar took Jerusalem; his son Joshua (Jeshua) became high priest of the returned exiles beside Zerubbabel.
know: Father of Joshua the high priest of the restoration

name: Solomon
summary: Solomon, son of David and Bathsheba (named Jedidiah, 'beloved of the LORD'), was anointed king through Nathan, Zadok and Bathsheba. At Gibeon he asked God for a listening heart to judge the people and received wisdom, riches and honour; his judgement between two mothers became proverbial. He built and dedicated the Temple in Jerusalem, where God's glory filled the house, and his fame drew the Queen of Sheba. But his many foreign wives turned his heart to other gods, and after his death the kingdom split.
catholic: Solomon's prayer at the dedication of the Temple is presented in the Catechism as a model of prayer: the Temple, the house of prayer David wanted to build, is the work of his son (CCC 2580). As son of David who builds God's house he fulfils 2 Sam 7:13 only in part; Jesus is the true Son of David and 'something greater than Solomon' (Mt 12:42) whose risen Body is the Temple (Jn 2:19-21). His prayer for wisdom (1 Kgs 3; Wis 9) is read on the 17th Sunday in Ordinary Time (Year A), and the wisdom books - Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, Song of Songs and Wisdom - are traditionally associated with him. His fall through idolatry is a warning that wisdom must be matched by fidelity.
know: Son of David and Bathsheba; also named Jedidiah
Asked God for wisdom at Gibeon
Built and dedicated the First Temple
Visited by the Queen of Sheba
Turned to idols in old age; the kingdom split after him

name: Naamah
summary: Naamah the Ammonitess, a wife of Solomon, was the mother of King Rehoboam and is named as queen mother in the regnal formula.

name: Hiram
summary: Hiram (Huram) king of Tyre sent cedar and craftsmen to build David's palace and made a treaty with Solomon, supplying cedar, cypress and skilled workers for the Temple in exchange for grain and oil. He partnered with Solomon's fleet to Ophir.
know: Supplied cedars of Lebanon for the Temple

name: Hiram the craftsman
summary: Hiram of Tyre, son of a widow of Naphtali (Chronicles: of Dan) and a Tyrian bronze-worker, cast the Temple's bronze pillars Jachin and Boaz, the bronze Sea and its furnishings. Chronicles calls him Huram-abi.
know: Made the pillars Jachin and Boaz

name: Queen of Sheba
summary: The Queen of Sheba heard of Solomon's fame and came to Jerusalem with camels bearing spices, gold and precious stones to test him with hard questions. Overwhelmed by his wisdom and the order of his house and worship, she blessed the LORD and exchanged rich gifts with the king.
catholic: Jesus says 'the Queen of the South' will rise at the judgement to condemn his generation, for she came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon, 'and behold, something greater than Solomon is here' (Mt 12:42). The Fathers saw in her the Gentile Church coming to Christ, and her gifts of gold and spices are linked with Psalm 72 and Isaiah 60 and the Magi's gifts at the Epiphany.
know: Came to test Solomon with riddles
Brought gold, spices and precious stones
Called 'Queen of the South' by Jesus

name: Hadad the Edomite
summary: Hadad, of the Edomite royal house, escaped Joab's massacre as a child, grew up in Egypt married to Pharaoh's sister-in-law, and returned to oppose Solomon.
know: Raised up by God as an adversary to Solomon

name: Rezon
summary: Rezon son of Eliada fled his master Hadadezer, became a raider chief, took Damascus and was an adversary of Israel all Solomon's days.

name: Shishak
summary: Shishak king of Egypt sheltered the fugitive Jeroboam and, in Rehoboam's fifth year, invaded Judah and carried off the treasures of the Temple and palace, including Solomon's golden shields.
know: Usually identified with Pharaoh Shoshenq I

name: Rehoboam
summary: Rehoboam son of Solomon and Naamah went to Shechem to be made king, but rejected the elders' advice and answered the people harshly - 'my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions' - so the ten northern tribes broke away under Jeroboam. Shemaiah stopped him from waging war on Israel. In his reign Shishak of Egypt plundered Jerusalem; he reigned seventeen years.
catholic: Rehoboam's folly fulfils Ahijah's prophecy and shows how pride divides God's people; the Church has often read the schism of Israel and Judah as a warning against division and a longing for the unity Christ restores (cf. Ezek 37:15-22; Jn 11:52). He is an ancestor of Jesus (Mt 1:7).
know: Son of Solomon and Naamah the Ammonitess
His harsh answer split the kingdom
Shishak plundered the Temple in his day

name: Maacah
summary: Maacah, granddaughter of Absalom (called 'daughter of Abishalom'), was Rehoboam's favourite wife and the mother of Abijah. She remained queen mother into the reign of Asa, who deposed her for making an abominable image for Asherah.
catholic: Maacah shows the real power of the gebirah (queen mother) in Judah - a power Asa could remove when it was used for idolatry. Her story is the negative counterpart to Bathsheba's role as intercessor.
know: Removed as queen mother by Asa for idolatry
Called Micaiah daughter of Uriel in 2 Chr 13:2

name: Abijah
summary: Abijah (Abijam) son of Rehoboam reigned three years. Kings judges him as walking in his father's sins, while Chronicles records his speech on Mount Zemaraim defending the Davidic covenant and the true priesthood before defeating Jeroboam.
know: Defeated Jeroboam after appealing to the 'covenant of salt' with David

name: Asa
summary: Asa son of Abijah reigned forty-one years and 'did what was right'. He removed idols and male cult prostitutes, deposed the queen mother Maacah for her Asherah image, and defeated Zerah the Ethiopian by relying on the LORD. Later he bribed Ben-hadad of Damascus against Baasha, imprisoned the seer Hanani who rebuked him, and in his foot disease sought physicians rather than the LORD.
know: Removed his grandmother Maacah as queen mother
Renewed the covenant after Azariah son of Oded's prophecy
Relied on Syria rather than God late in his reign

name: Azubah
summary: Azubah daughter of Shilhi, wife of Asa, was the mother of King Jehoshaphat.

name: Jehoshaphat
summary: Jehoshaphat son of Asa reigned twenty-five years and walked in the LORD's ways: he sent Levites to teach the law in the cities and appointed judges, charging them to judge in the fear of the LORD. He allied with Ahab by marriage and fought beside him at Ramoth-gilead, where Micaiah prophesied. Facing a great Moabite-Ammonite invasion he proclaimed a fast and sent singers ahead of the army, and God gave the victory.
catholic: Jehoshaphat's prayer 'we do not know what to do, but our eyes are on you' (2 Chr 20:12) and the victory won through praise are classic texts on trust and liturgical prayer. He is an ancestor of Jesus (Mt 1:8). His alliance with Ahab's house, sealed by marrying his son to Athaliah, nearly destroyed David's line.
know: Sent teachers of the law through Judah
Won a battle led by singers

name: Jehoram (Joram) of Judah
summary: Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat married Athaliah, Ahab's daughter, and walked in the ways of Ahab's house. On taking the throne he killed all his brothers. Edom and Libnah revolted; a letter from Elijah foretold his punishment, and he died of a terrible disease of the bowels, 'to no one's regret'.

name: Athaliah
summary: Athaliah, daughter of Ahab (granddaughter of Omri), married Jehoram of Judah and was queen mother of Ahaziah. When Jehu killed her son, she seized the throne and massacred the royal family, but the infant Joash was hidden by Jehosheba. After six years the priest Jehoiada crowned Joash in the Temple, and Athaliah, crying 'Treason!', was put to death.
catholic: Athaliah's attempt to wipe out the seed of David nearly broke God's promise to David; its preservation in one hidden child is a striking instance of God's fidelity to the Davidic covenant, which Catholic readers trace on to Christ. She is the only woman to rule Judah as sovereign.
know: Wife of Jehoram, mother of Ahaziah
Usurped the throne for six years

name: Ahaziah of Judah
summary: Ahaziah son of Jehoram and Athaliah reigned one year, following the counsel of his mother and Ahab's house. Visiting the wounded Joram of Israel at Jezreel, he was caught up in Jehu's revolt and killed.

name: Jehosheba
summary: Jehosheba (Jehoshabeath), daughter of King Jehoram, sister of Ahaziah and wife of the priest Jehoiada, rescued her infant nephew Joash from Athaliah's massacre and hid him in the Temple for six years.
catholic: By saving the last heir of David, Jehosheba preserved the line from which the Messiah would come; she is often compared to the women who protected Moses and to the Holy Family's flight from Herod's massacre.
know: Hid Joash in the Temple six years

name: Jehoiada
summary: Jehoiada the priest, husband of Jehosheba, guarded the hidden Joash in the Temple and in the seventh year organised the guard, crowned and anointed the boy king, had Athaliah executed, destroyed the temple of Baal and renewed the covenant. Joash did right all his days; Jehoiada died at 130 and was buried among the kings.
know: Buried among the kings of Judah

name: Zechariah son of Jehoiada
summary: After Jehoiada's death the princes of Judah turned to idols; Jehoiada's son Zechariah, clothed by the Spirit of God, rebuked them, and at King Joash's command he was stoned in the Temple court, crying 'May the LORD look on it and avenge it'.
catholic: Jesus speaks of the blood of the righteous 'from Abel to Zechariah', killed between the sanctuary and the altar (Mt 23:35; Lk 11:51) - a reference generally taken to this Zechariah, the last murder recorded in the last book of the Hebrew canon. Matthew calls him 'son of Barachiah', a difficulty discussed since the Fathers. He prefigures the martyrs and Christ, the prophet rejected in the Temple.
know: Spoke by the Spirit of God
Stoned in the Temple court at Joash's command

name: Zibiah
summary: Zibiah of Beersheba was the mother of King Joash (Jehoash) of Judah.

name: Joash (Jehoash) of Judah
summary: Joash son of Ahaziah, hidden as a baby from Athaliah, was crowned at seven by Jehoiada and reigned forty years. He repaired the Temple with a collection chest while Jehoiada lived, but afterwards turned to idols, had Zechariah son of Jehoiada stoned, paid off Hazael of Syria with the Temple treasures, and was murdered by his servants.
know: Turned to idols after Jehoiada died

name: Jehoaddin
summary: Jehoaddin (Jehoaddan) of Jerusalem was the mother of King Amaziah.

name: Amaziah
summary: Amaziah son of Joash reigned twenty-nine years. He executed his father's assassins but, following the law, spared their children; he defeated Edom in the Valley of Salt but then worshipped Edom's gods. Provoking Jehoash of Israel to battle, he was defeated and Jerusalem's wall broken; he was later murdered at Lachish.
know: Spared the assassins' children per Deut 24:16
Defeated Edom, then adopted its gods

name: Jecoliah
summary: Jecoliah (Jechiliah) of Jerusalem was the mother of King Uzziah (Azariah).

name: Uzziah (Azariah)
summary: Uzziah, also called Azariah, became king at sixteen and reigned fifty-two years. He prospered while he sought God - building towers, organising the army and loving the soil - but in pride he entered the Temple to burn incense, a priestly act; when the priests resisted he was struck with leprosy and lived isolated until death while his son Jotham governed.
catholic: Isaiah's great vision of the thrice-holy God came 'in the year that King Uzziah died' (Isa 6:1); the seraphim's Sanctus is sung at every Mass. Uzziah's leprosy for usurping the priest's office is often cited to show that priesthood is received, not seized (cf. Heb 5:4). He is in Jesus' genealogy (Mt 1:8-9).
know: Struck with leprosy for offering incense
Isaiah's call came the year he died

name: Azariah the priest
summary: Azariah the chief priest, with eighty priests, confronted King Uzziah when he tried to burn incense in the Temple, and drove him out when leprosy broke out on his forehead.
know: Withstood the king in the sanctuary

name: Jerusha
summary: Jerusha daughter of Zadok was the wife of Uzziah and mother of King Jotham.

name: Jotham
summary: Jotham son of Uzziah governed during his father's leprosy and then reigned sixteen years. He did right, built the upper gate of the Temple and subdued the Ammonites, 'because he ordered his ways before the LORD', though the people still sacrificed on the high places.
know: Built the upper gate of the Temple
Isaiah, Hosea and Micah prophesied in his time

name: Ahaz
summary: Ahaz son of Jotham reigned sixteen years and did evil, even making his son pass through the fire. When Rezin of Syria and Pekah of Israel attacked Jerusalem, he refused Isaiah's call to trust God and ask a sign, and instead made himself a vassal of Tiglath-pileser of Assyria, copying a Damascus altar for the Temple and closing the Temple's doors.
catholic: To the faithless Ahaz Isaiah gave the sign: 'Behold, the virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel' (Isa 7:14), which Matthew sees fulfilled in the virginal conception of Jesus (Mt 1:22-23); the Church reads it on the 4th Sunday of Advent (Year A). Ahaz, who would not ask a sign, thus stands at the threshold of the great Marian prophecy.
know: Refused to ask a sign of the LORD
Copied a pagan altar for the Temple

relations.type: received the sign of the virgin

name: Abi
summary: Abi (Abijah) daughter of Zechariah was the wife of Ahaz and mother of King Hezekiah.

name: Hezekiah
summary: Hezekiah son of Ahaz reigned twenty-nine years and trusted the LORD like no king before or after. He reopened and purified the Temple, held a great Passover inviting even the north, and destroyed the high places and Moses' bronze serpent Nehushtan, which had become an idol. When Sennacherib besieged Jerusalem he spread the Assyrian letter before the LORD and, encouraged by Isaiah, saw the city delivered. Healed from mortal illness with the sign of the retreating shadow, he then showed his treasures to Babylonian envoys, and Isaiah foretold exile to Babylon.
catholic: Hezekiah's prayer and Isaiah's support during Sennacherib's siege are classic examples of trust in God; his canticle of thanksgiving after his healing (Isa 38:10-20) is prayed in the Liturgy of the Hours. Sirach praises him with David and Josiah as the only faithful kings (Sir 49:4), and he is in Jesus' genealogy (Mt 1:9-10). Proverbs 25:1 credits 'the men of Hezekiah' with collecting proverbs of Solomon.
know: Restored the Temple and the Passover
Healed with 15 more years of life

name: Hephzibah
summary: Hephzibah was the wife of Hezekiah and mother of King Manasseh.
know: Her name ('my delight is in her') is later used of Zion in Isa 62:4

name: Manasseh
summary: Manasseh son of Hezekiah reigned fifty-five years, the longest of any king of Judah, and was its most wicked: he rebuilt the high places, set altars to the host of heaven in the Temple, burned his son as an offering, practised sorcery and 'shed very much innocent blood'. Kings blames the Exile on his sins; Chronicles adds that he was taken in chains to Babylon, humbled himself and prayed, and was restored, then removed foreign gods.
catholic: Manasseh's repentance in captivity (2 Chr 33:12-13) shows that no sinner is beyond God's mercy. The 'Prayer of Manasseh', a penitential prayer attributed to him, appears in some Bibles and in the appendix of the Clementine Vulgate but is not part of the Catholic canon. Jewish and Christian tradition hold that Isaiah was martyred under him. He is in Jesus' genealogy (Mt 1:10).
know: Filled Jerusalem with idolatry and innocent blood
Taken captive to Babylon and repented (Chronicles)
His sins are given as the cause of the Exile

name: Meshullemeth
summary: Meshullemeth daughter of Haruz of Jotbah was the wife of Manasseh and mother of King Amon.

name: Amon
summary: Amon son of Manasseh continued his father's idolatry for two years until his servants killed him in his house; the people of the land executed the conspirators and made his son Josiah king.

name: Jedidah
summary: Jedidah daughter of Adaiah of Bozkath was the wife of Amon and mother of King Josiah.

name: Josiah
summary: Josiah son of Amon became king at eight and reigned thirty-one years, the great reforming king. While the Temple was being repaired the high priest Hilkiah found the book of the law; Josiah tore his clothes, consulted the prophetess Huldah, read the covenant to the people and renewed it, purged idolatry from Jerusalem to Bethel (fulfilling a prophecy made three centuries earlier) and celebrated an unequalled Passover. He was killed at Megiddo opposing Pharaoh Necoh, and Jeremiah lamented him.
catholic: Josiah is praised as having no equal in turning to the LORD 'with all his heart, soul and might' (2 Kgs 23:25) - the words of the Shema - and Sirach says his memory is 'like incense' (Sir 49:1). His reform shows renewal flowing from the rediscovered Word of God and the liturgy (Passover). He stands in Jesus' genealogy (Mt 1:10-11), and the mourning for him at Megiddo is recalled in Zechariah 12:11, a text John applies to the Pierced One.
know: The book of the law was found in his reign
Renewed the covenant and purged idolatry
Killed by Pharaoh Necoh at Megiddo

name: Hamutal
summary: Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah was a wife of Josiah and mother of two kings, Jehoahaz and Zedekiah.
know: Her father is not the prophet Jeremiah

name: Zebidah
summary: Zebidah daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah was a wife of Josiah and mother of King Jehoiakim.

name: Johanan son of Josiah
summary: Johanan is listed as Josiah's firstborn but never reigned.

name: Jehoahaz of Judah
summary: Jehoahaz (Shallum), son of Josiah, was made king by the people after Megiddo but reigned only three months before Pharaoh Necoh deposed him and took him to Egypt, where he died.

name: Jehoiakim
summary: Jehoiakim (Eliakim), son of Josiah, was installed by Pharaoh Necoh and taxed the land to pay him; he then served Nebuchadnezzar and rebelled. He persecuted the prophets, killing Uriah son of Shemaiah, and cut up and burned Jeremiah's scroll in his brazier column by column. He reigned eleven years.
catholic: Jehoiakim burning the scroll of God's word (Jer 36) is the classic image of a heart that refuses God's word - while the word itself, rewritten, endures. Daniel 1:1 dates the first deportation, including Daniel, to his reign. Matthew's genealogy passes over him.

name: Nehushta
summary: Nehushta daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem, wife of Jehoiakim, was queen mother of Jehoiachin and went into exile with him to Babylon.
know: Taken to Babylon with her son
Jeremiah addressed 'the king and the queen mother' (Jer 13:18)

name: Jehoiachin
summary: Jehoiachin (Jeconiah, Coniah), son of Jehoiakim, reigned three months at eighteen before surrendering Jerusalem to Nebuchadnezzar in 597 BC. He was taken to Babylon with his mother, officials, craftsmen and the Temple treasures. Jeremiah declared that none of his offspring would sit on David's throne, yet after thirty-seven years Evilmerodach released him from prison and gave him a seat at the king's table - a sign that David's line endured.
catholic: Matthew's genealogy names 'Jechoniah' at the Babylonian exile and continues through his son Shealtiel to Zerubbabel and on to Joseph (Mt 1:11-12), showing that God kept his promise to David even through the Exile. His release from prison at the end of 2 Kings is a quiet note of hope for the Davidic line. Ezekiel dates his visions by 'King Jehoiachin's captivity' (Ezek 1:2).

name: Zedekiah
summary: Zedekiah (Mattaniah), son of Josiah and uncle of Jehoiachin, was installed by Nebuchadnezzar and renamed. Weak and vacillating, he consulted Jeremiah secretly yet let him be imprisoned, and finally rebelled against Babylon. After an eighteen-month siege Jerusalem fell in 587/586 BC; Zedekiah fled, was captured near Jericho, saw his sons killed at Riblah, was blinded and taken to Babylon in chains.
catholic: Zedekiah is the tragic end of the earthly Davidic kingship - a king who knew God's word through Jeremiah but lacked courage to obey it. The end of the monarchy turns Israel's hope toward the promised righteous Branch of David (Jer 23:5-6; 33:15), fulfilled in Christ (2 Chr 36 is read on the 4th Sunday of Lent, Year B).

name: Malchiram
summary: Malchiram is listed among the sons of Jehoiachin (Jeconiah) the captive.

name: Shenazzar
summary: Shenazzar is listed among the sons of Jehoiachin (Jeconiah) the captive.

name: Jekamiah
summary: Jekamiah is listed among the sons of Jehoiachin (Jeconiah) the captive.

name: Hoshama
summary: Hoshama is listed among the sons of Jehoiachin (Jeconiah) the captive.

name: Nedabiah
summary: Nedabiah is listed among the sons of Jehoiachin (Jeconiah) the captive.

name: Pedaiah
summary: Pedaiah son of Jehoiachin is named in the Hebrew text of 1 Chr 3:19 as the father of Zerubbabel, whereas Ezra, Haggai and the Gospels call Zerubbabel 'son of Shealtiel'.
know: Possible explanations: levirate marriage, or Zerubbabel was Shealtiel's legal heir

name: Nebat
summary: Nebat, an Ephraimite of Zeredah, was the father of Jeroboam I, who is constantly called 'Jeroboam the son of Nebat'.
know: His name became a byword through his son

name: Zeruah
summary: Zeruah, a widow, was the mother of Jeroboam I.

name: Jeroboam I
summary: Jeroboam son of Nebat, an able Ephraimite overseer under Solomon, was told by the prophet Ahijah, who tore his new cloak into twelve pieces, that he would rule ten tribes. He fled to Shishak in Egypt, returned after Solomon's death and became first king of the northern kingdom. To keep the people from going to Jerusalem he set up golden calves at Bethel and Dan with non-Levitical priests and his own feast - 'the sin of Jeroboam' by which every later northern king is judged.
catholic: Jeroboam's calves - a political religion cut off from the Temple and the lawful priesthood - became the paradigm of schism in Scripture. Catholic commentators have long drawn from his story the lesson that unity of worship and lawful priesthood belong to God's covenant, a theme fulfilled in Christ's prayer 'that they may all be one' (Jn 17:21).
know: Ahijah tore a cloak into 12 pieces for him
First king of the northern kingdom
Set up golden calves at Bethel and Dan
'The sin of Jeroboam' became a refrain in Kings
His house was wiped out by Baasha

name: Abijah son of Jeroboam
summary: Abijah, Jeroboam's young son, fell sick; his mother went in disguise to the blind prophet Ahijah, who foretold the child's death - the only one of Jeroboam's house to be mourned and buried, 'because in him there is found some good thing toward the LORD'.
know: The only good found in Jeroboam's house

name: Nadab
summary: Nadab son of Jeroboam reigned two years and was assassinated by Baasha while besieging Gibbethon; Baasha then exterminated Jeroboam's house as Ahijah had prophesied.

name: Baasha
summary: Baasha son of Ahijah, of Issachar, killed Nadab, wiped out Jeroboam's house and reigned twenty-four years at Tirzah, warring with Asa of Judah; yet he walked in Jeroboam's sins, and the prophet Jehu son of Hanani foretold the same end for his house.
know: Usurper who founded Israel's second dynasty
Condemned by Jehu son of Hanani

name: Elah
summary: Elah son of Baasha reigned two years; while getting drunk at Tirzah he was murdered by his chariot commander Zimri, who destroyed Baasha's house.

name: Zimri
summary: Zimri, commander of half the chariots, killed Elah and reigned seven days at Tirzah; when the army made Omri king and besieged the city, Zimri burned the palace over himself.
know: 'Zimri, murderer of his master' became a taunt (2 Kgs 9:31)

name: Tibni
summary: Tibni son of Ginath was backed by half of Israel as king against Omri; after some years of civil war Tibni died and Omri reigned alone.

name: Omri
summary: Omri, army commander, was made king after Zimri's coup, overcame Tibni and reigned twelve years. He bought the hill of Samaria and built it as Israel's new capital, founding a powerful dynasty, but did more evil than all before him.
know: Founder of the dynasty of Ahab
Known in Assyrian records ('house of Omri')

name: Ahab
summary: Ahab son of Omri reigned twenty-two years in Samaria and 'did more to provoke the LORD' than all the kings before him. He married Jezebel of Sidon, built a temple and altar to Baal, and clashed repeatedly with the prophet Elijah - over the drought, on Mount Carmel, and after Jezebel had Naboth murdered for his vineyard. He won victories over Ben-hadad but spared him, ignored Micaiah's warning, and died at Ramoth-gilead from a random arrow, the dogs licking his blood as Elijah had foretold.
catholic: Ahab is Scripture's image of the weak ruler led by a wicked spouse into idolatry and injustice; Naboth's vineyard, retold by St. Ambrose in 'On Naboth', became a classic text on the sin of greed and abuse of the poor. Yet when Ahab humbled himself at Elijah's word, God delayed the disaster (1 Kgs 21:27-29) - a sign of God's readiness to show mercy even to great sinners.
know: Son of Omri; husband of Jezebel
Opposed by Elijah, called 'troubler of Israel'

name: Ethbaal
summary: Ethbaal king of the Sidonians was the father of Jezebel, Ahab's queen.

name: Jezebel
summary: Jezebel, daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians, married Ahab and zealously promoted the worship of Baal, killing the LORD's prophets and maintaining 850 prophets of Baal and Asherah. She vowed to kill Elijah after Carmel and arranged Naboth's judicial murder with false witnesses. At Jehu's revolt she painted her eyes and taunted him from a window, and was thrown down and eaten by dogs as Elijah had foretold.
catholic: Jezebel became a byword for seductive idolatry - Revelation calls a false prophetess at Thyatira 'Jezebel' (Rev 2:20). Her persecution of Elijah is a type of the world's hostility to God's prophets, as Herodias's hostility to John the Baptist, the 'Elijah who was to come', has long been compared to it.
know: Had Naboth killed by false witness
Thrown from a window at Jehu's command

name: Ahaziah of Israel
summary: Ahaziah son of Ahab reigned two years. After falling through a lattice he sent to inquire of Baal-zebub, god of Ekron; Elijah intercepted the messengers, called down fire on two companies of soldiers, and foretold the king's death. He died without a son.

name: Joram (Jehoram) of Israel
summary: Joram (Jehoram) son of Ahab reigned twelve years. He campaigned with Jehoshaphat against Mesha of Moab, when Elisha provided water; the king of Israel in the stories of Naaman and the siege of Samaria is probably he. Wounded at Ramoth-gilead, he was killed by Jehu at Naboth's plot in Jezreel, ending Ahab's dynasty.
know: Son of Ahab and brother of Ahaziah
Killed by Jehu's arrow on Naboth's land

name: Jehu
summary: Jehu son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi, an army commander famous for driving 'furiously', was anointed king by a disciple of Elisha, as God had told Elijah at Horeb. He killed Joram of Israel and Ahaziah of Judah, had Jezebel thrown down, wiped out Ahab's house, and slaughtered the worshippers of Baal in their temple. Yet he kept Jeroboam's calves; God promised his sons the throne to the fourth generation.
catholic: Jehu carries out God's judgement on Ahab's house as Elijah foretold, but Hosea condemns 'the blood of Jezreel' (Hos 1:4) - zeal for God's cause cannot excuse cruelty or a divided heart. The Fathers use him as an example of zeal that stops halfway.
know: Anointed at Ramoth-gilead by Elisha's disciple
His dynasty lasted four more generations

name: Jehoahaz of Israel
summary: Jehoahaz son of Jehu reigned seventeen years, during which Hazael and Ben-hadad of Syria crushed Israel's army; he sought the LORD, who gave Israel a deliverer.
know: Israel reduced to 50 horsemen and 10 chariots

name: Jehoash (Joash) of Israel
summary: Jehoash son of Jehoahaz reigned sixteen years. He wept over the dying Elisha - 'my father, the chariots of Israel' - and at the prophet's word shot the arrow of victory and struck the ground three times, winning three victories over Syria. He defeated Amaziah of Judah, broke down Jerusalem's wall and plundered the Temple.
know: Struck the ground only three times

name: Jeroboam II
summary: Jeroboam II son of Jehoash reigned forty-one years, the most prosperous of Israel's kings, restoring its borders from Hamath to the Dead Sea as the prophet Jonah son of Amittai had foretold. Yet his reign's wealth and injustice drew the denunciations of Amos and Hosea.
know: Restored Israel's borders as Jonah prophesied
Amos and Hosea prophesied in his day

name: Zechariah
summary: Zechariah son of Jeroboam II reigned six months before Shallum killed him publicly, ending Jehu's dynasty in the fourth generation as the LORD had promised.

name: Shallum
summary: Shallum son of Jabesh killed Zechariah and reigned one month in Samaria before Menahem killed him.

name: Menahem
summary: Menahem son of Gadi killed Shallum, savagely put down resistance at Tiphsah, and reigned ten years, paying Pul (Tiglath-pileser) of Assyria a thousand talents of silver raised from Israel's wealthy men.

name: Pekahiah
summary: Pekahiah son of Menahem reigned two years before his officer Pekah killed him in the palace at Samaria.

name: Pekah
summary: Pekah son of Remaliah killed Pekahiah and reigned in Samaria. Allied with Rezin of Damascus he attacked Ahaz of Judah - the crisis of Isaiah's Immanuel prophecy - but Tiglath-pileser took Galilee and much of Israel, and Hoshea assassinated him.
catholic: Isaiah dismisses Rezin and 'the son of Remaliah' as 'two tails of smoking firebrands' (Isa 7:4), the setting of the Immanuel sign.
know: Called 'the son of Remaliah' by Isaiah

name: Hoshea
summary: Hoshea son of Elah killed Pekah and became the last king of Israel. A vassal of Shalmaneser of Assyria, he conspired with Egypt and withheld tribute; Shalmaneser imprisoned him and besieged Samaria for three years, and in 722 BC Samaria fell and Israel was deported to Assyria.
catholic: 2 Kings 17 explains the fall of Samaria as the fruit of centuries of idolatry and rejection of the prophets - a sober theological meditation the Church reads as a call to fidelity.
know: Last king of the northern kingdom
Samaria fell in his ninth year (722 BC)

name: Ahijah the Shilonite
summary: Ahijah, a prophet of Shiloh, met Jeroboam outside Jerusalem, tore his new cloak into twelve pieces and gave him ten, announcing that God would give him ten tribes because of Solomon's idolatry. Years later, old and blind, he recognised Jeroboam's disguised wife and foretold the death of her son and the destruction of Jeroboam's house.
know: Tore his cloak into twelve pieces
Foretold the division of the kingdom
His prophecy is cited as a source for Solomon's history

name: Shemaiah
summary: Shemaiah the man of God told Rehoboam not to fight the northern tribes, 'for this thing is from me', and the army went home. When Shishak invaded he told Judah's leaders they had forsaken God; they humbled themselves and were spared complete destruction.
know: Prevented civil war after the schism
Called Judah to repentance before Shishak

name: Iddo the seer
summary: Iddo the seer is cited by Chronicles as an author of visions concerning Jeroboam and of records of Rehoboam and Abijah.
know: A lost prophetic source used by the Chronicler

name: Azariah son of Oded
summary: Azariah son of Oded, filled with the Spirit of God, met Asa returning from victory and told him 'the LORD is with you while you are with him', prompting Asa's reform and covenant renewal.
know: His prophecy led to Asa's reform

name: Hanani the seer
summary: Hanani the seer rebuked King Asa for relying on the king of Syria instead of the LORD - 'the eyes of the LORD run back and forth throughout the whole earth' - and was put in the stocks for it.

name: Jehu son of Hanani
summary: The prophet Jehu son of Hanani pronounced God's judgement on Baasha of Israel, and decades later rebuked Jehoshaphat of Judah for helping the wicked Ahab; he also wrote a history of Jehoshaphat.

name: Elijah
summary: Elijah the Tishbite of Gilead burst onto the scene announcing a drought to Ahab. Fed by ravens at the brook Cherith and by the widow of Zarephath, whose son he raised, he confronted the 450 prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel, where fire fell from heaven on his sacrifice. Fleeing Jezebel, he was fed by an angel and walked forty days to Horeb, where God came not in wind, earthquake or fire but in 'a still small voice'. He called Elisha, condemned Ahab over Naboth, and was taken up to heaven in a whirlwind with a chariot of fire.
catholic: Elijah is the 'father' of the prophets; the Catechism presents his prayer and Carmel sacrifice as a model of prayer and conversion (CCC 2582-2583), and his fire from heaven as a figure of the fire of the Holy Spirit (CCC 696). Malachi foretold his return before the day of the LORD, and Jesus identifies John the Baptist as the Elijah who was to come (Mt 11:14; 17:10-13; cf. Lk 1:17; CCC 718). At the Transfiguration Moses and Elijah, the Law and the Prophets, speak with Jesus of his exodus (CCC 555). The angel's bread that strengthened him for forty days is read with the Bread of Life discourse (19th Sunday, Year B) as a figure of the Eucharist, and his forty-day journey shapes Lent. The Carmelite Order venerates him as its spiritual father and model of contemplation; his feast is July 20.
know: Raised the widow of Zarephath's son
Defeated the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel
Heard God in the 'still small voice' at Horeb
Taken up in a whirlwind with a chariot of fire
Appeared with Moses at the Transfiguration

name: Widow of Zarephath
summary: During the drought God sent Elijah to a Gentile widow at Zarephath in Sidon who was gathering sticks to bake a last meal for herself and her son. She gave Elijah her little cake first, and her jar of flour and jug of oil did not fail until the rain came. When her son died, Elijah stretched himself on the child three times and the LORD restored his life.
catholic: Jesus cites her in his Nazareth sermon (Lk 4:25-26) - Elijah was sent to none of Israel's widows but to her - as a sign that God's mercy reaches the Gentiles; the passage is read on the Monday of the 3rd week of Lent. Her gift from her poverty is paired liturgically with the widow's mite (32nd Sunday, Year B), and the unfailing flour and oil have been read as a figure of the Eucharist. The Catechism notes that Elijah taught her to believe in God's word (CCC 2583).
know: Fed Elijah with her last flour and oil
Her flour and oil did not run out
Her son was raised by Elijah

name: Obadiah
summary: Obadiah, who 'feared the LORD greatly', was in charge of Ahab's household; when Jezebel was killing the prophets he hid a hundred of them in two caves and fed them. He arranged Elijah's meeting with Ahab before Carmel.
catholic: Some Jewish tradition identified him with the prophet Obadiah, but Scripture does not. He is a model of the believer who serves faithfully and courageously within a hostile court.

name: Naboth
summary: Naboth of Jezreel refused to sell Ahab his ancestral vineyard: 'The LORD forbid that I should give the inheritance of my fathers to you.' Jezebel had him falsely accused of cursing God and the king, and he was stoned outside the city; Elijah then pronounced doom on Ahab and Jezebel.
catholic: St. Ambrose's treatise 'On Naboth' made him a classic figure in Catholic social teaching against the greed of the powerful, and the Fathers saw in him a type of Christ: an innocent man condemned by false witnesses on a charge of blasphemy and executed outside the city.
know: Refused to sell his ancestral inheritance
