His blood was avenged on Ahab's house

name: Micaiah son of Imlah
summary: Micaiah son of Imlah was the one prophet Ahab hated 'because he never prophesies good concerning me'. Before the battle of Ramoth-gilead he first mocked the court prophets' message, then foretold Ahab's death and revealed a lying spirit in their mouths; struck by Zedekiah son of Chenaanah, he was imprisoned on bread and water.
catholic: Micaiah - 'what the LORD says to me, that I will speak' - is a model of prophetic integrity against the pressure of a court consensus, foreshadowing Christ struck before the high priest.
know: Saw the LORD on his throne with the host of heaven

name: Imlah
summary: Imlah was the father of the prophet Micaiah.

name: Zedekiah son of Chenaanah
summary: Zedekiah son of Chenaanah, leader of Ahab's court prophets, made iron horns to promise victory at Ramoth-gilead and struck Micaiah on the cheek.
know: Made iron horns as a sign

name: Shaphat
summary: Shaphat of Abel Meholah was the father of the prophet Elisha.
know: Elisha left his oxen to follow Elijah

name: Elisha
summary: Elisha son of Shaphat was ploughing with twelve yoke of oxen when Elijah cast his mantle on him; he slaughtered the oxen, fed the people and followed. He asked for a double portion of Elijah's spirit, saw him taken up, and parted the Jordan with his mantle. For some fifty years he worked many miracles - purifying Jericho's spring, multiplying a widow's oil, raising the Shunammite's son, feeding a hundred men with twenty loaves, healing Naaman, making an axe-head float - advised kings, anointed Jehu through a disciple, and foretold Hazael's rule. Even after death a corpse touching his bones came to life.
catholic: Elisha's miracles foreshadow Christ's: the feeding of a hundred with twenty barley loaves 'and some was left over' (2 Kgs 4:42-44) is read with Jesus' feeding of the five thousand (17th Sunday, Year B); the raising of the Shunammite's son near Shunem anticipates Jesus raising the widow's son at nearby Nain (Lk 7:11-17); and the cleansing of Naaman in the Jordan prefigures Baptism (Lk 4:27). His call - leaving everything to follow Elijah - is read with Jesus' demands on would-be disciples (13th Sunday, Year C). The dead man revived by touching his bones (2 Kgs 13:21) has long been cited in support of the veneration of relics. The Roman Martyrology commemorates him on June 14.
know: Called while ploughing with 12 yoke of oxen
Received a double portion of Elijah's spirit
A dead man revived on touching his bones

name: Gehazi
summary: Gehazi, Elisha's servant, suggested the Shunammite's reward and carried the prophet's staff to her son. After Elisha refused Naaman's gifts, Gehazi ran after him, lied to obtain silver and clothing, and was struck with Naaman's leprosy. Later he told the king of Elisha's great deeds.
catholic: Gehazi's attempt to profit from a gift of God is often paired with Simon Magus (Acts 8) as the archetype of simony, the sin of trading in spiritual things.
know: Took silver from Naaman by deceit
Recounted Elisha's miracles to the king

name: The Shunammite woman
summary: A wealthy woman of Shunem persuaded Elisha to eat at her house and, with her husband, built him a small upper room. Elisha promised her a son; years later the boy died in her lap, and she rode to Mount Carmel, clung to Elisha's feet and would not leave him until he came and raised the child. Warned of famine, she lived seven years in Philistia, and the king restored her land.
catholic: Her hospitality to the man of God is read on the 13th Sunday in Ordinary Time (Year A) with Jesus' words 'whoever receives a prophet...'. The raising of her son anticipates Jesus raising the widow's son at Nain, near Shunem (Lk 7:11-17), and her faith - 'It is well' - is a model of trust in grief.
know: Received a son by Elisha's promise
Her son was raised from the dead
Her land was restored by the king

name: Naaman
summary: Naaman, commander of the army of the king of Syria, was a mighty man but a leper. A captive Israelite girl told his wife about the prophet in Samaria; Elisha sent word to wash seven times in the Jordan. After angry resistance he obeyed, and his flesh became like a little child's. He confessed that there is no God in all the earth but in Israel, and took two mule-loads of earth to worship the LORD at home.
catholic: Naaman's cleansing in the Jordan is a classic Old Testament figure of Baptism, read in the Fathers (Ambrose, 'On the Mysteries') and in the liturgy: the humble washing restores him like a newborn child. Jesus cites him as a Gentile healed when many in Israel were not (Lk 4:27, read on the Monday of the 3rd week of Lent), and his story is paired with the healed Samaritan leper (28th Sunday, Year C). His conversion shows God's salvation offered to all nations.
know: Learned of Elisha from a captive Israelite girl
Washed seven times in the Jordan

name: Mesha
summary: Mesha king of Moab, a great sheep-breeder, rebelled against Israel after Ahab's death; besieged by Israel, Judah and Edom, he sacrificed his eldest son on the city wall and the invaders withdrew.
know: Also known from the Moabite Stone (Mesha Stele)

name: Ben-hadad I
summary: Ben-hadad son of Tabrimmon son of Hezion, king of Syria at Damascus, broke his treaty with Baasha of Israel when Asa of Judah bribed him with Temple treasure, and ravaged northern Israel.

name: Ben-hadad
summary: Ben-hadad king of Syria besieged Samaria under Ahab and was twice defeated; Ahab spared him, against the LORD's will. In Elisha's day he again besieged Samaria, sought Elisha's capture at Dothan, and when sick sent Hazael to ask Elisha whether he would recover; Hazael smothered him and seized the throne.
know: Defeated by Ahab, who spared him

name: Hazael
summary: God told Elijah at Horeb to anoint Hazael king over Syria. Sent by the sick Ben-hadad to Elisha, Hazael watched the prophet weep at the evil he would do to Israel; the next day he smothered Ben-hadad and reigned. He cruelly oppressed Israel under Jehu and Jehoahaz and threatened Jerusalem until Joash paid him off.

name: Ben-hadad son of Hazael
summary: Ben-hadad son of Hazael lost three battles and the captured towns to Jehoash of Israel, as Elisha's arrows had foretold.

name: Rezin
summary: Rezin king of Damascus allied with Pekah of Israel to attack Ahaz of Judah, the crisis behind Isaiah's Immanuel prophecy. Ahaz called in Tiglath-pileser, who took Damascus and killed Rezin.

name: Jehonadab son of Rechab
summary: Jehonadab son of Rechab joined Jehu in his chariot to witness his 'zeal for the LORD' against Baal. Generations later his descendants, the Rechabites, still kept his command to drink no wine and live in tents, and Jeremiah held up their fidelity as a rebuke to Judah.
catholic: The Rechabites' fidelity to their ancestor's rule (Jer 35) has been seen by spiritual writers as an Old Testament anticipation of religious rules of life; the Carmelites, who claim Elijah as their father, have also appealed to them.
know: His descendants' obedience is praised in Jeremiah 35

name: Huldah
summary: Huldah the prophetess, wife of Shallum keeper of the wardrobe, lived in the Second Quarter of Jerusalem. When Josiah's officials brought her the newly found book of the law, she confirmed God's coming judgement on Judah but promised that Josiah, because his heart was tender, would die in peace before it.
catholic: Huldah is one of the few women named as prophets in the Old Testament (with Miriam and Deborah); Josiah's officials sought God's word through her, showing that prophetic charism is given to women as well as men - a gift the Church recognises in the Virgin Mary and in women saints and Doctors of the Church.
know: Authenticated the book of the law
Foretold judgement and Josiah's peaceful death

name: Shallum son of Tikvah
summary: Shallum son of Tikvah, keeper of the wardrobe, was the husband of Huldah the prophetess.

name: Eliakim son of Hilkiah
summary: Eliakim son of Hilkiah, 'over the household' of King Hezekiah, led the delegation that met the Rabshakeh outside Jerusalem's wall and carried the Assyrian threats to Hezekiah and Isaiah. Isaiah prophesied that he would replace Shebna and receive 'the key of the house of David'.
catholic: Isaiah's oracle - 'I will lay the key of David's house on his shoulder; he will open and no one will shut' (Isa 22:22) - lies behind Jesus' gift of the keys of the kingdom to Peter (Mt 16:19) and is applied to Christ himself in Revelation 3:7. Catholic interpreters see in Eliakim's office of royal steward, with father-like authority over the household, a type of the Petrine office (Isa 22:20-24 is read with Mt 16:13-20 on the 21st Sunday, Year A).
know: Royal steward ('over the household') under Hezekiah
Received 'the key of the house of David' in Isaiah's oracle

name: Shebna
summary: Shebna was a high official of Hezekiah - 'over the house' in Isaiah, scribe in Kings - whom Isaiah condemned for carving himself a grand tomb and told that Eliakim would replace him.
know: Rebuked by Isaiah for his pride
Part of the delegation to the Rabshakeh

name: Joah son of Asaph
summary: Joah son of Asaph was Hezekiah's recorder and one of the three officials who met the Rabshakeh.

name: Shaphan
summary: Shaphan son of Azaliah, Josiah's scribe, received the book of the law from Hilkiah and read it before the king. His family were Jeremiah's protectors: his son Ahikam and grandson Gedaliah.
know: Read the rediscovered law to Josiah

name: Ahikam
summary: Ahikam son of Shaphan was among Josiah's delegation to Huldah, and later protected Jeremiah from being put to death.

name: Gedaliah
summary: After the fall of Jerusalem Nebuchadnezzar appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam governor over those left in Judah, with his seat at Mizpah, and Jeremiah went to live with him. He urged the people to serve Babylon and live, but ignored warnings and was assassinated by Ishmael son of Nethaniah, after which the remnant fled to Egypt.
know: His murder is remembered by the Jewish Fast of Gedaliah

name: Ishmael son of Nethaniah
summary: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, of the royal family, murdered Governor Gedaliah and his companions at Mizpah, then fled to the Ammonites when Johanan son of Kareah pursued him.

name: Johanan son of Kareah
summary: Johanan son of Kareah warned Gedaliah of the plot against him and then rescued Ishmael's captives; fearing Babylon, he led the remnant to Egypt against Jeremiah's word, taking Jeremiah with them.

name: Tiglath-pileser
summary: Tiglath-pileser (III) of Assyria, called Pul in 2 Kings 15:19, received tribute from Menahem, conquered Galilee and Gilead under Pekah and deported their people, and answered Ahaz's appeal by taking Damascus.

name: Shalmaneser
summary: Shalmaneser (V) of Assyria made Hoshea his vassal, imprisoned him for treachery and besieged Samaria for three years until it fell. Tobit calls him Enemessar.

name: Sennacherib
summary: Sennacherib king of Assyria invaded Judah in Hezekiah's fourteenth year, took its fortified cities and sent the Rabshakeh to demand Jerusalem's surrender, mocking the LORD. After Hezekiah's prayer, the angel of the LORD struck the Assyrian camp, and Sennacherib returned to Nineveh, where his sons killed him while he worshipped in the temple of Nisroch.
know: His army was struck by the angel of the LORD
Killed by his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer

name: The Rabshakeh
summary: The Rabshakeh (a high Assyrian title, 'chief cupbearer') stood by the conduit of the upper pool and, speaking Hebrew so the people on the wall would hear, mocked Hezekiah's trust in the LORD and demanded surrender.

name: Tirhakah
summary: Tirhakah king of Ethiopia (Cush) marched out against Sennacherib during the siege of Jerusalem.

name: Adrammelech
summary: Adrammelech, son of Sennacherib, killed his father with Sharezer and fled to Ararat.

name: Sharezer
summary: Sharezer, son of Sennacherib, killed his father with Adrammelech and fled to Ararat.

name: Esarhaddon
summary: Esarhaddon succeeded his murdered father Sennacherib; he settled foreign peoples in Samaria, and Tobit (calling him Sarchedonus) says he made Achiacharus (Ahikar), Tobit's nephew, second to himself.

name: Merodach-baladan
summary: Merodach-baladan (Berodach Baladan) son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent envoys and a gift to the recovered Hezekiah, who showed them all his treasures - prompting Isaiah's prophecy that everything would be carried to Babylon.

name: Necoh
summary: Pharaoh Necoh (Neco) marched north to aid Assyria; Josiah went out against him at Megiddo and was killed. Necoh then deposed Jehoahaz, made Jehoiakim king and laid tribute on Judah, until Nebuchadnezzar defeated him at Carchemish.

name: Nebuchadnezzar
summary: Nebuchadnezzar (II) king of Babylon defeated Egypt at Carchemish, made Jehoiakim his vassal, deported Jehoiachin and the elite of Jerusalem in 597 BC, installed Zedekiah, and after Zedekiah's revolt destroyed Jerusalem and Solomon's Temple in 587/586 BC, carrying the people into exile. In Daniel he dreams of the great statue, throws the three young men into the furnace, is humbled by madness and finally praises the Most High.
catholic: Jeremiah calls Nebuchadnezzar God's 'servant' (Jer 25:9) - an instrument of judgement who does not know he serves God's purpose. In Daniel 4 his humiliation and restoration show God's sovereignty over the proud kingdoms of the world, and the stone 'cut without hands' that shatters his dream-statue (Dan 2:34-35, 44) is read by the Fathers as Christ and his everlasting Kingdom, the stone born of the Virgin without human father. The Nebuchadnezzar of the Book of Judith, 'king of the Assyrians', is generally read as a literary figure of the arrogant world-power.
know: Destroyed Jerusalem and the Temple (587/586 BC)
Deported Jehoiachin, Daniel and Ezekiel's generation
Dreamed of the statue and the stone (Dan 2)
Cast the three young men into the furnace (Dan 3)

name: Nebuzaradan
summary: Nebuzaradan, captain of Nebuchadnezzar's guard, burned the Temple, the palace and the houses of Jerusalem, broke down its walls and led the people into exile; by the king's order he freed Jeremiah and let him choose where to live.

name: Evilmerodach
summary: Evilmerodach (Amel-Marduk), Nebuchadnezzar's successor, released Jehoiachin from prison in the first year of his reign, spoke kindly to him and gave him a place at the king's table for life. Historically he was Nebuchadnezzar's son, though Scripture does not say so.
